title: Kinship, Caste and Class: Early Societies (c. 600 BCE-600 CE)

topics.title: The Critical Edition of the Mahabharata

concepts.learning_objective: Describe how the Critical Edition of the Mahabharata was prepared between 1919 and 1966.
Explain what the regional variations in Mahabharata manuscripts reveal about social history.

topics.title: Kinship and Marriage: Many Rules and Varied Practices

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the ideal of patriliny and its importance for succession in ruling families.
Distinguish between exogamy, endogamy, polygyny and polyandry and the Brahmanical forms of marriage.
Analyse how Satavahana inscriptions show departures from Brahmanical gotra rules.

topics.title: Social Differences: Within and Beyond the Framework of Caste

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the occupations prescribed for the four varnas and stories that upheld them.
Evaluate the evidence that political power did not depend on Kshatriya birth.
Explain the nature of jatis, guilds and the treatment of groups placed outside the varna order.
Explain how access to property differed between men and women.
Analyse how the Buddhist tradition questioned status based on varna by pointing to wealth.
Interpret Sangam poems that show chiefs were expected to share their resources.

topics.title: Explaining Social Differences: A Social Contract

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the Buddhist myth of the mahasammata in the Sutta Pitaka.
Evaluate the implications of the idea that kingship rested on human choice.

topics.title: Handling Texts: Historians and the Mahabharata

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish the narrative and didactic sections of the Mahabharata and the meaning of itihasa.
Identify the authors and phases of composition of the Mahabharata.
Evaluate how historians compare the epic with archaeological and social evidence.
Explain how the Mahabharata grew through versions, retellings and performances.
Analyse how Mahashweta Devi's retelling raises questions the Sanskrit text is silent on.
